scope: Refactor only the MU Desk Cursor Gallery module to the accepted definition, visual system, and system packaging contracts.

owned_files.change: Merge keyed MU shared resources without globally restyling unrelated windows.
New keyed WPF tokens and controls implementing MU Product Standard 1.0.0.
Replace the equal-card wall with the accepted collection-detail composition and complete states.
Own selection, detail, feedback, keyboard focus, and real loading/error state transitions.
Preserve one on-demand window and MU Desk error forwarding.
Implement accepted target-path migration, explicit load errors, atomic metadata writes, backup, apply, and reset behavior.
Expose existing completeness, role preview, missing-role, import-note, and current-state data to the view.
New pure, testable helper for selecting and atomically establishing the MU Desk library copy.
Replace only the Cursor Gallery module-card symbol and copy needed for the accepted module identity.
New production module icon exports generated from the approved icon direction.
Add deterministic migration and compatibility tests without touching the real user registry or cursor library.

preserve: All 17 existing skin packages and their cursor/preview paths remain reachable.
Applying a skin continues to update current-user cursor registry roles and refresh Windows.
Missing roles continue to fall back to Windows Aero/default values.
The gallery remains an on-demand window with no independent process, tray, startup item, settings, version, or installer.
MU Desk remains the only user-facing shell.
Errors remain real and visible; no fixture or demo data substitutes for a failed library.
migrations: On first use, atomically copy legacy %AppData%\CursorSkinManager\library.json when the new target does not exist.
Do not move or delete the legacy JSON, cursor files, preview files, or storage directories.
Write library.bak.json before modifying applied-state metadata in the MU Desk copy.
When migration cannot establish the target, keep legacy read compatibility and expose the real error.
implementation_sequence: Add keyed MU WPF tokens and shared control styles; merge them without changing unrelated windows.
Add the pure library migration helper and deterministic tests.
Refactor CursorLibraryService to use the accepted target/legacy path contract and explicit result/error states.
Extend CursorSkinPackage presentation data without changing the serialized compatibility shape.
Refactor CursorGalleryWindow into the accepted list-detail layout and state matrix.
Preserve CursorGalleryModule single-window and error-forwarding behavior.
Produce the approved Cursor Gallery icon family and add required exports.
Wire the module icon and accepted copy into the Cursor Gallery window and its MU Desk card.
Build, run focused tests, exercise both entry points, inspect visual geometry and keyboard focus, and verify no child process remains.
Record acceptance evidence and restore any cursor registry values changed during a controlled integration check.

risks.risk: Legacy JSON can contain absolute paths that no longer exist.
risks.mitigation: Preserve paths, show incomplete/missing roles, and never discard packages merely because individual files are absent.

risks.risk: Migration could diverge from a legacy application that still writes the old library.
risks.mitigation: Copy only once, leave the legacy source untouched, and document MU Desk as the writer after migration.

risks.risk: Registry integration testing can alter the user's current cursor scheme.
risks.mitigation: Test core logic with fakes; for one controlled integration check, snapshot the exact current-user cursor values and restore that snapshot rather than assuming Windows default.

risks.risk: Shared WPF resources could unintentionally restyle other modules.
risks.mitigation: Use keyed MU styles and apply them explicitly only inside Cursor Gallery during this scope.

risks.risk: Seventeen role previews can create nested overflow or poor scaling.
risks.mitigation: Keep one named scroll region per collection/detail, verify 100% and 200% Windows scaling, and reject page-level horizontal scrolling.

build: Release build and all existing Toolbox, MouseRing, and DesktopOrganizer tests pass.
tests: New target already exists: no legacy copy and target is selected.
New target missing plus valid legacy library: atomic copy succeeds and source remains.
Migration failure: real error is returned and no successful empty library is reported.
Malformed JSON surfaces an error without overwriting either source.
CursorSkinPackage serialization remains compatible with the existing camelCase library.
windows_and_surfaces: Open from MU Desk module card and from tray; both reuse one Cursor Gallery window.
All 17 packages remain reachable and one selected package exposes its role previews.
Current, incomplete, missing-role, empty, loading, success, and failure states are distinguishable.
Close the gallery and verify no child process or WebView remains.
system_integration: Verify target/legacy path selection against disposable fixture directories.
Verify registry operations are current-user only.
If an actual apply check is performed, snapshot and restore the exact prior cursor registry state.
accessibility: Keyboard can move through the skin list, reveal detail, reach Apply and Reset, and show visible focus.
Selection and current state do not rely on color alone.
Labels remain legible at 200% Windows scaling and reduced motion is respected.
visual: Reject horizontal page scrolling, clipped previews, oversized empty cards, and hidden primary action.
Confirm inherited MU tokens, charcoal outline, violet selection, and no legacy blue card-wall styling.
